newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower, drinks shares slump.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower, drinks shares slump.

text.p: French stocks opened lower on Friday in a decline led by shares in drinks companies after the government announced plans to raise "sin taxes" as part of a fiscal reform programme unveiled on Thursday evening.
Trading, whose start was delayed by 20 minutes due to technical problems, was thin and nervous ahead of the U.S. August unemployment report due out this afternoon.
A trader said the market was pleased with the government's tax reform proposals, entailing big income tax cuts, "but the U.S. jobs figure will probably have a bigger impact."
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 9.60 points, or 0.48 percent, at 1,986.63 at 0855 GMT, while the September CAC-40 futures contract was down 14 points at 1,989.

Shares in drinks companies fell after Finance Minister Jean Arthuis confirmed on Friday that taxes on alcohol and tobacco would be increased. Shares in LVMH were down 0.74 percent and Remy Cointreau's stock was 0.5 percent lower.
Shares in Pernod Ricard, which depends more heavily on its home market, were down 1.25 percent at 292.30.
Tobacco group Seita was 0.9 percent lower at 197 francs.
